decisions.quote:
Although our results do not cast any doubt on the robustness of the red-anger effect in

within-subjects designs, we did not observe the red-anger effect at first impression, which

suggests that demand characteristics have been driving the effect. Thus, we consider previous

findings to be a method-dependent phenomenon.
decisions.reason: The authors replicate the original red-anger effect in within-subjects designs across both Study 1 (close replication) and Study 2 (conceptual replication), while demonstrating via suspicion checks and a between-subjects absence-of-demand condition that the effect vanishes when demand characteristics are eliminated. Because the paper's central message and overall conclusion are that the replicated effect is an artifact of demand characteristics in the original within-subjects method, the special verdict 'statistically successful but flawed' applies.
